record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.original_question: Is the Buscher T-duality transformation in the time direction, which maps the Schwarzschild black hole to a massless solution with only primary scalar hair while preserving the supersymmetry properties in the low-energy analysis, a legitimate string symmetry; and if it is not, how should the resulting massless purely scalar solution of the low-energy effective action be interpreted?

evidence.quote: A Buscher T duality transformation in the time direction preserves the SUSY properties and asymptotic behavior of the solution giving new asymptotically flat solution with no unbroken supersymmetries: precisely the massless solution with only primary scalar hair written above in Eqs. (25,26).
All that happened in this transformation is that the mass M, which does appear in the B bound has completely transformed in primary dilaton charge Qd which in principle does not.

It can be argued that the duality transformation that takes us from Schwarzschild's BH (for which a string theory model is still lacking) to the massless purely scalar solution, and which we have use heuristically, is not a good string symmetry, but that would not change the fact that the massless purely scalar solution is a solution of the low-energy effective action at least as good as Schwarzschild's.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the low-energy effective action of heterotic string theory in four dimensions, restricted to the gravity–dilaton sector (with the antisymmetric tensor field set to zero), with action
S = ∫ d^4x √(-g) e^{-2φ} ( R + 4 (∂φ)^2 ),
in the "string frame", where g_{μν} is the spacetime metric and φ is the dilaton.

The Schwarzschild solution, written in string-frame coordinates as
ds^2 = -(1 - 2M/r) dt^2 + (1 - 2M/r)^{-1} dr^2 + r^2 dΩ^2,    φ = 0,
is an exact solution of this action. Applying the Buscher T-duality transformation along the time-like Killing vector ∂_t — i.e., the formal Buscher rules
g_{tt} → 1/g_{tt},   e^{-2φ} → e^{-2φ}/|g_{tt}|,
with the remaining metric components unchanged — produces a new asymptotically flat, static, spherically symmetric solution of the same low-energy effective action which is everywhere massless (ADM mass zero) and carries only "primary" dilaton (scalar) charge Q_d, with the original mass parameter M of the Schwarzschild solution reappearing entirely as the dilaton charge Q_d of the dual configuration. In the low-energy supergravity analysis this transformation preserves the (absence of) unbroken supersymmetries and the asymptotic behavior.

Questions:
(a) Is this time-like Buscher T-duality transformation a legitimate symmetry of the full (non-perturbative) string theory, in the same sense that ordinary space-like Buscher T-duality is?
(b) If it is not a genuine string symmetry, how should the resulting purely scalar, massless solution of the low-energy effective action — which saturates no Bogomol'nyi bound involving the mass while still being an exact solution — be physically interpreted within string theory?
artifact.category_tag: Time-like T-duality and black hole hair
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of whether the time-like Buscher T-duality mapping Schwarzschild to the massless primary-scalar-hair solution is a genuine string symmetry, nor a settled physical interpretation of the dual massless scalar configuration. Time-like T-duality is known to be subtle (it is connected to type II*/E-theories rather than ordinary type II/heterotic strings), but no specific source clearly resolves the question as posed. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to T-Duality in String Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Standard review of Buscher T-duality rules for NS-NS sector; the abelian Buscher procedure applies to any isometry, including time-like, at the level of the sigma-model, but global/quantum legitimacy is not addressed here.
status_evidence.claim: Buscher rules are derived for generic abelian isometries, leaving open the status of time-like applications.

status_evidence.title: T-duality (nLab)
status_evidence.snippet: Encyclopedic discussion of T-duality emphasizing space-like circle compactifications; time-like T-duality is mentioned as relating to type II* theories rather than as a standard string equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Time-like T-duality is not on the same footing as space-like T-duality in the standard formulation.
